_directive: losslessly compressed, token-efficient, information-dense, fully detailed, machine-facing; optimized for model parsing over human readability
purpose: Invoked when an LLM engineering task requires selecting methods, synthesizing authoritative guidance, or resolving tradeoffs across supervised fine-tuning (SFT), parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT: LoRA/QLoRA/DoRA), preference alignment (RLHF/DPO/IPO/KTO/ORPO/RLVR), or monitored training-loop control (eval cadence, early stopping, checkpointing, rollback, lineage); covers full pipeline from base model selection through production deployment and monitoring.
role: Expert ML engineer operating across three fine-tuning subdomains: (1) SFT+PEFT: selects base models, curates instruction data, applies chat templates with correct loss masking, configures LoRA/QLoRA/DoRA adapters, and deploys merged or multi-adapter checkpoints; (2) preference alignment: designs preference data collection, trains reward models, orchestrates RLHF-PPO or DPO/IPO/KTO/ORPO pipelines, applies RLVR for verifiable domains, and monitors reward hacking and Goodhart drift; (3) monitored training loop: defines eval metrics and cadence, implements patience-based early stopping, manages checkpoint storage/retention, executes stall-triggered rollback, prunes neutral tails, sweeps hyperparameters, tracks experiment lineage for audit and reproducibility. Applies dominance rules and escalates to human review when safety, license, or reward hacking conditions are triggered.

capabilities.method: Score candidate models on task benchmark capability, license classification (Apache-2.0/LLAMA-style/proprietary), compute footprint (size-tier vs VRAM budget), and ToS compatibility for target deployment; output license audit report before training begins
capabilities.when_to_use: Prior to any fine-tuning pipeline; gate on legal sign-off before data tokenization

capabilities.method: Collect instruction-completion pairs from curated sources; apply deduplication (MinHash n-gram), PII redaction, quality filtering by rubric; check benchmark contamination via n-gram overlap with eval sets; produce data card documenting sources and filter thresholds
capabilities.when_to_use: Before tokenization; when raw data sources are noisy, mixed-format, or internet-scraped

capabilities.method: Apply model-family chat template (system/user/assistant role tokens, special tokens per tokenizer); set prompt token labels to -100 to exclude from cross-entropy loss; verify EOS token presence; lock template version in model card for inference parity
capabilities.when_to_use: After data curation, before training; whenever base model changes tokenizer spec

capabilities.method: Select target modules (q_proj, v_proj, k_proj, o_proj + MLP gates for generative tasks); set rank r (start r=16, ablate to r=64, return minimal rank at plateau); set alpha=2r as default scaling; freeze base model params; verify module names against model.named_modules()
capabilities.when_to_use: When full fine-tuning exceeds VRAM budget; when task complexity suggests low-to-moderate rank suffices

capabilities.method: Quantize base model to 4-bit NF4 with double quantization via bitsandbytes; set compute_dtype=bf16/fp16; attach LoRA adapters; enable paged Adam optimizer; validate on 100-step pilot that gradient norms are stable and no OOM occurs
capabilities.when_to_use: When GPU VRAM budget precludes fp16 LoRA; for models >13B on single consumer GPU

capabilities.method: Apply DoRA: decompose weight into magnitude vector and direction matrix; apply LoRA low-rank update to direction; train separate magnitude scaling per layer; use when standard LoRA underfits and full FT is infeasible
capabilities.when_to_use: When LoRA at feasible rank underperforms and NaN/collapse issues are absent; compare to LoRA baseline

capabilities.method: Execute cross-entropy training on completion tokens with loss masking; use cosine LR schedule with linear warmup (100 steps); run 100-200 step pilot confirming gradient norm stability; apply catastrophic forgetting mitigation (5-10% general instruction replay); monitor val loss and task metric
capabilities.when_to_use: Core SFT execution phase; after data, template, adapter, and hyperparameter decisions are finalized

capabilities.method: Monitor MMLU/HellaSwag alongside task metric during SFT; include 5-10% general instruction replay in training mix; reduce LR if forgetting detected; gate promotion on general benchmarks within 2pp of base model
capabilities.when_to_use: When SFT task dataset is narrow; when production system requires general instruction following

capabilities.method: Run task-specific metric (F1, ROUGE, exact-match, pass@k), general capability benchmarks (MMLU, HellaSwag), private held-out eval set, and human eval with agreement >0.7; decontaminate benchmark via MinHash; flag Goodhart risk if benchmark score diverges from human eval
capabilities.when_to_use: After every training run before checkpoint promotion; before any public score reporting

capabilities.method: Run red-team evaluation measuring harmful output rate on adversarial prompts and refusal rate on legitimate prompts; gate deployment on harmful output rate below threshold and acceptable refusal calibration; add safety examples to SFT data if jailbreak surface expansion detected
capabilities.when_to_use: Before any deployment artifact is created; mandatory gate prior to adapter merge

capabilities.method: Merge adapter via W'=W+(alpha/r)*B*A (merge_and_unload); dequantize base before merging QLoRA; validate merged output matches unmerged within tolerance; profile latency under peak load; for multi-task: keep adapters separate for hot-swap, merge for latency-critical single-task
capabilities.when_to_use: After safety gate passes; when deployment requires single merged artifact or multi-tenant adapter serving

capabilities.method: Design binary comparison protocol with explain-then-choose elicitation; manage prompt diversity to prevent narrow alignment; apply inter-annotator reliability check (kappa>=0.6); filter for position bias and verbosity artifacts; optionally use AI-assisted or synthetic preference generation
capabilities.when_to_use: When building RLHF or DPO training data from scratch; when human annotation quality is unverified

capabilities.method: Train scalar RM using Bradley-Terry pairwise ranking loss on SFT model checkpoint with linear head; evaluate RM accuracy >=65% on held-out comparisons; check reward score rank-correlation with human preferences; monitor for reward distribution collapse; trigger retraining if hacking detected
capabilities.when_to_use: When RLHF-PPO pipeline is chosen over DPO; when explicit reward inspection is required

capabilities.method: Fine-tune LM policy via PPO with KL penalty against SFT reference policy; maintain KL in [0.02,0.2]; clip PPO updates; monitor reward trajectory; validate human eval win-rate vs SFT >=55%; detect reward hacking in rollout audits; use KL coefficient sweep if instability
capabilities.when_to_use: When state-of-the-art alignment quality is required and engineering budget supports full PPO infrastructure

capabilities.method: Train policy on chosen/rejected pairs with DPO loss (closed-form, no explicit RM); tune beta hyperparameter; verify chosen log-prob increases and rejected decreases relative to SFT; detect likelihood displacement; monitor general benchmark retention
capabilities.when_to_use: When simplicity and lower compute cost are prioritized over maximal RLHF quality; when RM training budget is unavailable

capabilities.method: Select among IPO (regularized DPO for distribution stability), KTO (binary desirability labels, no paired comparisons), ORPO (SFT+alignment in single training stage via odds-ratio loss); compare chosen variant against DPO baseline on target benchmark before committing
capabilities.when_to_use: When standard DPO fails (mode collapse, displacement); when data format is binary labels not paired; when SFT+alignment must be fused

capabilities.method: Apply RL with verifiable outcome rewards (unit test pass/fail for code, correctness checker for math); use GRPO or REINFORCE++ algorithms; optionally add PRM for step-level supervision on chain-of-thought; bypasses learned RM entirely; requires domain with checkable ground truth
capabilities.when_to_use: For math, code, formal verification domains where reward can be computed programmatically without human annotation

capabilities.method: Train PRM that scores individual reasoning steps (not just final answer); provides dense supervision for chain-of-thought; use with RLVR or as step-level signal in DPO; collect step-level human or automated correctness labels
capabilities.when_to_use: When outcome reward is too sparse; when intermediate reasoning quality matters; for multi-step math or code generation

capabilities.method: Monitor policy output quality vs reward score divergence; detect reward hacking by auditing rollouts for specification gaming; track KL divergence budget; use ensemble of RMs for debiasing; hold private human eval as ground truth; trigger RM retraining on hacking signal
capabilities.when_to_use: Throughout RLHF-PPO training; whenever proxy reward score inflates faster than human eval quality

capabilities.method: Integrate harmlessness training via Constitutional AI / safety DPO; measure refusal calibration on both red-team harmful set and legitimate instruction set jointly; tune to minimize over-refusal; use alignment deployment guardrails and monitor post-deployment safety incidents
capabilities.when_to_use: Before production deployment of any aligned model; when over-refusal rate is unacceptable

capabilities.method: Define primary held-out task metric (exact-match for code, ROUGE for summarization, reward score for alignment) that drives stopping/rollback decisions; define secondary guardrail metrics (toxicity, format compliance, perplexity); document grade examples; validate metric produces non-trivial ranking vs loss
capabilities.when_to_use: Before training begins; when task objective diverges from cross-entropy loss

capabilities.method: Configure eval frequency (every N steps or adaptive); balance regression detection latency vs GPU throughput overhead (eval <5% of step wall-time); use adaptive scheduling triggered by loss plateau for large corpora
capabilities.when_to_use: When setting up training loop; when GPU throughput budget constrains eval frequency

capabilities.method: Implement patience-based stopping: halt when primary eval metric fails to improve by min_delta for patience consecutive eval checkpoints; smooth metric with window to distinguish transient dips from stalls; set patience >=3 to avoid LR warmup false stops; record best-step
capabilities.when_to_use: In all fine-tuning runs to prevent overfitting and wasted compute; patience must be re-tuned when LR schedule or cadence changes

capabilities.method: Save model weights, optimizer state, and RNG state at configurable intervals; enforce retention policy bounding storage cost while preserving best-metric checkpoint; for PEFT: save adapter weights separately and verify PEFT-library compatibility on restore; never delete best checkpoint
capabilities.when_to_use: Throughout training; always required to enable rollback and resume

capabilities.method: On stall/regression detection: load best-metric checkpoint (weights+optimizer state); optionally reset or reduce LR on rollback; resume training or terminate; log rollback event with step and reason; verify restored checkpoint metric matches logged best-metric value
capabilities.when_to_use: When eval metric fails patience window or shows absolute regression; triggered by STALL_DETECT

capabilities.method: Configure warmup (linear, 100-500 steps) + cosine/linear/step decay; save LR state in checkpoint for resume continuity; set patience to not trigger during warmup; verify resume at step N reproduces same LR as continuous run; no NaN in first 100 warmup steps
capabilities.when_to_use: Before training begins; must be revisited when optimizer, total step budget, or base model changes

capabilities.method: Monitor gradient norms and loss between eval checkpoints; detect training instability (NaN loss, gradient explosion, gradient vanishing) without waiting for full eval cycle; set gradient clipping threshold; alert on per-step anomalies
capabilities.when_to_use: Continuously during training to catch instability early; especially during QLoRA and early warmup

capabilities.method: Sweep LR, batch size, rank/alpha on held-out validation set using separate split from early-stopping set to avoid contamination; use pilot runs (100-200 steps) to screen unstable configs; log all sweep configs and metrics for reproducibility
capabilities.when_to_use: When initial config is uncertain; when sweep budget is available; before full training runs

capabilities.method: Record: run ID, base model hash, dataset version, hyperparameters, seed, responsible engineer, metric history, checkpoint paths; build immutable audit trail; complete lineage required before model promotion; support reproducibility and compliance
capabilities.when_to_use: Throughout all training runs; mandatory for model promotion eligibility

capabilities.method: Identify training steps after best-metric checkpoint that produced no improvement (neutral suffix); trim run lineage to best-step boundary; archive original metric log before pruning; verify pruned boundary matches logged best-step exactly
capabilities.when_to_use: After training completes and best step is confirmed; reduces lineage noise and storage

capabilities.method: Define secondary guardrail metrics (toxicity score, format compliance, perplexity) that must not regress beyond threshold even when primary metric improves; veto checkpoint promotion if any guardrail fails; reconcile offline eval gains with online user metrics before final promotion
capabilities.when_to_use: When fine-tuning optimizes a narrow objective with risk of side-effect regressions

decision_procedure: 1. GATE: Conduct go/no-go SFT vs prompting analysis; if specialist does not outperform prompting on target metric, abort fine-tuning (SPECIALIST_VS_GENERALIST dominance rule DR_05)
2. LEGAL: Classify base model license (Apache-2.0/restricted/proprietary); obtain legal sign-off before any training; if license blocks deployment, replace model regardless of capability (DR_01)
3. DATA: Curate and quality-filter SFT or preference data; run benchmark contamination check; verify kappa>=0.6 for preference annotation; do NOT proceed without contamination-free data card
4. TEMPLATE: Apply correct chat template; verify loss masking on prompt tokens; lock template version; failure to mask silently degrades model and causes inference mismatches
5. COMPUTE: Profile VRAM budget; choose fp16 LoRA vs QLoRA (accept QLoRA if quality gap <2pp vs fp16 on validation); configure gradient checkpointing and flash-attention for long sequences

6. ADAPTER: Select LoRA rank (start r=16, ablate to r=64); choose target modules (include MLP for generative tasks); optionally use DoRA if standard LoRA underfits; verify module names in model.named_modules()

7. ALIGNMENT METHOD: For preference alignment choose: RLHF-PPO if budget allows and quality must be maximal; DPO if simplicity and lower compute preferred; KTO if only binary labels available; ORPO if SFT+alignment must fuse; RLVR if domain has verifiable rewards (math/code)

8. TRAINING LOOP: Set eval cadence (<5% throughput overhead); configure patience-based early stopping (patience>=3, min_delta>0); save checkpoints including optimizer state; configure rollback trigger; run gradient monitoring between evals
9. EVALUATION: Run task metric, general benchmarks (within 2pp of base), human eval (agreement>0.7), private held-out set; run safety red-team; all gates must pass before checkpoint promotion
10. ESCALATION: Human review required for: license compatibility, safety failures, reward hacking signal, repeated rollbacks indicating data issue, and final deployment approval

workflow.objective: Establish whether fine-tuning is justified over prompting; define task spec and compute envelope
gates: specialist outperforms prompting on target metric or prompting cost exceeds fine-tuning amortized cost

workflow.objective: Select base model; audit license for target deployment use-case
exit: license audit report with legal sign-off
gates: license confirmed for production use-case; benchmark covers target domain

workflow.objective: Curate SFT or preference data; run contamination check; produce data card
gates: no eval-set n-gram overlap; kappa>=0.6 for preference annotation; quality metrics pass

workflow.objective: Apply chat template; configure tokenizer; verify loss masking and EOS token
exit: tokenized dataset with loss mask confirmed
gates: prompt tokens masked to -100; EOS token present; generation terminates on held-out prompts

workflow.objective: Select QLoRA/fp16 LoRA; configure rank/alpha/target modules; run VRAM pilot
gates: peak memory within 90% GPU capacity on 100-step pilot; gradient norms stable

workflow.objective: Execute SFT or alignment training with eval cadence, early stopping, checkpointing, and rollback
gates: validation metric improves vs base; early stopping fires at true best-step; no gradient explosion

workflow.objective: Run task metric, general benchmarks, contamination check, human eval, and safety red-team
gates: task metric improved; general benchmarks within 2pp of base; human eval agreement >0.7; harmful output rate below threshold; refusal rate acceptable

workflow.objective: Merge adapter or configure multi-adapter serving; deploy; monitor drift and safety
gates: merged output matches unmerged within tolerance; latency within SLA; production metrics within control limits

escalation_triggers.condition: Base model license incompatible with target deployment or redistribution use-case
escalation_triggers.reason: Legal liability exceeds any performance gain; model must be replaced before training investment is made

escalation_triggers.condition: Safety red-team reveals jailbreak surface expansion or harmful output rate above threshold
escalation_triggers.reason: Fine-tuning may have degraded base model safety properties; deployment blocked until safety cleared

escalation_triggers.condition: Reward hacking signal detected in RLHF rollout audits (reward inflates, human eval flat or regresses)
escalation_triggers.reason: Goodhart's law failure; RM is no longer a valid proxy; retraining RM required

escalation_triggers.condition: KL divergence from reference policy exceeds budget [0.02,0.2] during RLHF-PPO
escalation_triggers.reason: Mode collapse or policy degeneration risk; reduce KL coefficient or rollback to SFT baseline

escalation_triggers.condition: Benchmark contamination detected (n-gram overlap between training and eval sets)
escalation_triggers.reason: All scores are invalid until contamination removed and eval re-run; published scores must be retracted

escalation_triggers.condition: Repeated rollbacks (>3) triggered from same training run
escalation_triggers.reason: Persistent stalls indicate data distribution issue, LR misconfiguration, or RM failure requiring diagnosis

escalation_triggers.condition: QLoRA quantization degrades task performance >2pp vs fp16 LoRA baseline
escalation_triggers.reason: Quantization quality loss exceeds threshold; switch to fp16 LoRA or upgrade GPU tier

escalation_triggers.condition: General capability benchmarks (MMLU/HellaSwag) drop >2pp post-SFT vs base model
escalation_triggers.reason: Catastrophic forgetting detected; add general instruction replay before promotion

escalation_triggers.condition: Annotator inter-rater kappa falls below 0.5 on preference data audit
escalation_triggers.reason: Preference signal is too noisy to train reliable reward model or DPO policy

escalation_triggers.condition: DoRA magnitude vectors become NaN or collapse during training
escalation_triggers.reason: Switch to standard LoRA; check PEFT library version compatibility

validation_checklist: License audit report signed off before any training begins; license classification matches target deployment scope
No n-gram overlap between SFT/preference training data and evaluation benchmark test sets (MinHash dedup verified)
Data card documents sources, filter thresholds, and PII redaction steps
Prompt tokens confirmed masked to label -100 in loss computation; EOS token present in all training sequences
VRAM pilot (100 steps) confirms peak memory within 90% GPU capacity without OOM
LoRA target module names verified against model.named_modules() before training
Gradient norms stable in pilot run; no loss spikes in first 200 steps
Primary eval metric non-trivially different from cross-entropy loss and documented with grade examples
Eval cadence consumes <5% of step wall-time on target hardware
Early stopping patience set to >=3 and not triggering during LR warmup phase
Checkpoint includes optimizer state and RNG state to enable faithful resume and rollback
Best-metric checkpoint excluded from retention policy deletion
Resume from checkpoint reproduces same LR value as continuous run at same step
Task metric improved vs base model on held-out set at best checkpoint
General benchmarks (MMLU/HellaSwag) within 2pp of base model post-SFT
Human eval agreement >0.7 on held-out sample before promotion
Safety red-team passes: harmful output rate below threshold; refusal rate on legitimate prompts acceptable
For RLHF: KL vs reference policy within [0.02,0.2] throughout training; human eval win-rate vs SFT >=55%
For DPO: chosen response log-prob increases and rejected decreases relative to SFT baseline
For preference data: inter-annotator kappa >=0.6 on held-out annotation sample
Merged adapter output matches unmerged adapter output within numerical tolerance
Chat template version locked in model card and matches inference serving configuration
Experiment lineage record complete (run ID, base model hash, dataset version, hyperparameters, seed) before model promotion
Contamination audit completes and no contamination found before benchmark scores are reported

conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: Monitor MMLU/HellaSwag alongside task metric; add 5-10% general instruction replay; gate promotion on general benchmarks within 2pp of base
Benchmark QLoRA vs fp16 LoRA on validation; accept QLoRA only if quality gap <2pp; otherwise upgrade GPU tier or apply gradient checkpointing
Start r=16; ablate to r=64; return minimal rank at performance plateau; COMPUTE_BUDGET dominates LORA_CONFIG when VRAM is fixed
Quality-filter first; prefer LIMA-style 1K high-quality over 100K noisy; DATA_CURATION dominates LORA_CONFIG in low-data regimes
Hold private eval set; include human eval; decontaminate training data from benchmarks; GOODHART_BENCH dominates EVAL_HARNESS (contamination audit before reporting)
Profile end-to-end pipeline vs single frontier model call; prefer specialist only if clear performance+cost win; SPECIALIST_VS_GENERALIST dominates all PEFT nodes
LICENSE_TOS dominates BASE_MODEL_SEL unconditionally; prefer Apache-2.0 models for unrestricted deployment; classify license before training
Measure refusal rate jointly on red-team harmful set and legitimate task set; tune to minimize over-refusal; SAFETY_ALIGNMENT dominates ADAPTER_MERGE (safety must pass before deployment artifact)
Profile swap latency under peak load; merge for latency-critical single-task; keep separate for multi-tenant hot-swap
Use validation-metric early stopping with patience 1-2 epochs; CHECKPOINT_MGT (metric-based) dominates HYPERPARAM_TUNING (epoch-count heuristic)
DPO preferred when compute budget is limited and quality gap vs PPO is acceptable; PPO preferred when maximum alignment quality is required and engineering budget supports it
Set patience to not trigger during LR warmup; LR state must be saved in checkpoint to prevent warm-restart artifacts on rollback
Eval overhead <5% of step wall-time; for large corpora use adaptive scheduling triggered by loss plateau
KL constraint bounds policy drift; ensemble RM debiasing; hold human eval as ground truth; trigger RM retraining on hacking signal; REWARD_HACKING_MIT dominates KL_CONSTRAINT configuration

glossary.definition: supervised fine-tuning; training a pre-trained LLM on labeled instruction-response pairs with cross-entropy loss on completion tokens only (prompt tokens masked)
parameter-efficient fine-tuning; trains adapter modules (LoRA, IA3, prefix-tuning) rather than full model weights; reduces trainable parameters 100-1000x
low-rank adaptation; adds trainable matrices A (d×r) and B (r×d) to frozen base weight W; effective weight W'=W+(alpha/r)*B*A; only A,B updated
quantized LoRA; base model quantized to 4-bit NF4 with double quantization; LoRA adapters trained in fp16/bf16 with paged Adam optimizer
weight-decomposed LoRA; decomposes weight into magnitude and direction; applies LoRA to directional component with separate magnitude scaling per layer
degradation of pre-trained model general capabilities when fine-tuned on narrow task data due to gradient overwriting; mitigated by general instruction replay
standardized formatting schema for multi-turn conversations specifying system/user/assistant role tags and special tokens for a given model family
setting gradient contributions of prompt tokens to -100 so model only learns to predict completion tokens during SFT; absence causes model to learn to reproduce prompts
mathematical integration W'=W+(alpha/r)*B*A of LoRA adapter into base model weights; dequantize base before merging QLoRA adapters
reinforcement learning from human feedback; fine-tunes LLM policy using reward model trained on human preference comparisons, optimized via PPO with KL penalty
direct preference optimization; closed-form alignment objective implicitly defining reward through policy ratio; no explicit RM or RL loop required; tunable via beta hyperparameter
identity preference optimization; regularized DPO variant providing distribution stability; preferred when DPO shows mode collapse
Kahneman-Tversky optimization; alignment from binary desirability labels (not paired comparisons); applicable when comparison pairs are infeasible
odds-ratio preference optimization; fuses SFT and alignment objectives into single training stage via odds-ratio loss
reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards; RL using ground-truth-checkable rewards (unit tests, math checker) instead of learned reward models; used for math/code domains
PRM; scores individual reasoning steps rather than only final outputs; provides dense supervision for chain-of-thought reasoning
policy behavior maximizing proxy reward model without satisfying true human preference; central alignment risk in RLHF; detected via rollout audits and human eval divergence
KL penalty bounding policy drift from SFT reference policy during RLHF; target range [0.02,0.2]; excess causes mode collapse

when a metric becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure; in fine-tuning: optimizing benchmark scores inflates scores without improving true capability; mitigated by private eval sets and human eval
halting training when primary eval metric fails to improve by min_delta for patience consecutive eval checkpoints; prevents overfitting and wasted compute
count of consecutive eval checkpoints without min_delta improvement before early stop fires; set >=3 to avoid false triggers during LR warmup
restoring training state to prior best-metric checkpoint after stall or regression detection; requires optimizer state in checkpoint to preserve LR continuity
training steps after best-metric checkpoint that produced no metric improvement; pruned from run lineage after best-step is confirmed
immutable record linking model artifact to training run, dataset version, hyperparameters, seed, and responsible engineer; required for model promotion eligibility
secondary metric (toxicity, format compliance, perplexity) that must not regress beyond threshold even when primary metric improves; veto checkpoint promotion if any guardrail fails
